meta.label: STAGE 1 ONLY - full-field scoring off newspaper inputs. PACE + SECTIONALS dropped, divisor 0.90, signals /13. COMBO unsourced at both meetings. No bias flags: Warwick rail TRUE (strength 0), Hawkesbury strength 0.5 after v13 multipliers. Carded prices - edge filter NOT run.

races.why: Ran second last start and carries 54kg, 2.5kg under every other main chance in an 800m dash where weight bites hardest. RTG 93 sits second-top behind a $3.90 favourite that has raced once and is having blinkers and a tongue-tie applied for the first time.

Two wins in his last five, gate 2 at a tight track, and 57.5kg after a 4kg claim. The two at the head of the market are Ever So Ready off a spell and Runaround Sue humping 62kg over 800m, which the v14 weight rule penalises hard at this trip.

RTG 95, second-highest in the race, and the rails gate in a big maiden field at a country circuit where getting a cheap run matters more than raw ability. Priced at nearly double the favourite for a rating gap of five points.
Won last start, RTG 98, and meets the favourite Luconi 5kg better at the weights off a 1.5kg claim. Same price as Luconi for a horse in winning form carrying five kilos less.
RTG 98 and ran second last start, so the profile is a horse holding form rather than one coming back to it. Flitgrove heads the market on RTG 100 but has to give weight away on a Soft 5.
Won two starts back and ran second last time, which is the shape the engine keeps missing at long prices. RTG 89 is modest and the wide gate is the reason the market has left it alone.

RTG 99 is a point off top and it ran third first-up, so second-up improvement is the live angle. A 2kg claim brings it to 58.5kg and it sits at a full point longer than the favourite for almost the same rating.

Won last start and drops to 56.5kg, three kilos under the top of the handicap. RTG 91 is the reason it is friendless at $16, but winning form at a light weight is the profile the archive says gets blocked.
Second last start off a consistent 35122 line, gate 4, and 57.5kg. The market has it eighth in betting on RTG 93 while three horses rated within five points of it are under $5.
Highest-rated live runner in the race on RTG 98 with the best recent line on the card. Carries no edge at $4.40 against a $4.20 favourite, so it is here as the form horse rather than a bet.

Three career starts for a win last time out, and meets the RTG 100 favourite Philatelic two kilos better. The gate is the one negative but a Good 4 with the rail out only 4m for part of the circuit barely punishes it.

Top-rated in the race on RTG 100, has won its last two, and carries only 57kg over 2000m. The barrier is the whole reason it is not favourite, and over this trip a wide draw costs far less than it does sprinting.
RTG 99, two runs for a second and a fourth, and the inside gate against Power Broker drawn ten. Rated the top of the card but priced accordingly, so it fails the edge test and is not a bet under v16.
RTG 97 and the rails gate in a 1100m fillies and mares maiden, where an inside draw and early speed decide most of them. Lucsain at $1.70 is rated three points higher and pays less than half.

Second-highest rated at RTG 93 and gets pre-race ear muffs for the first time, which is the one gear change on the card that points at a horse being managed rather than tinkered with. Not On My Watch is the obvious one at $2.00 and offers nothing.
RTG 98 with two wins in its last four and a gate inside the rail-out zone. Sprightly Affair is the $2.40 favourite off a spell and drawn nine, which is the wrong way round for a horse at that price.

Has already won over this course and distance and is first-up carrying 62kg after a 3kg claim. The weight is why it is $16, but a proven track-and-trip winner resuming is exactly the profile the old floor used to block.
Ran second on debut, drawn the rails, and carries 56kg. RTG 93 sits behind Made In Italy on 100 but the price gap is more than double, which is the divergence the engine is built to take.

RTG 97 is second-top in the race and the market has it eighth in at $18, entirely on the strength of a poor last run before a spell. First-up and unproven, so treated as an exotics line rather than a win bet.

Equal top-rated on RTG 100 and second-up after a quiet resuming run, yet sits at $23 while the other RTG 100 in the race is $2.90. The newspaper also has it as its own top selection, so the price is out of step with more than just this model.
